steps.prompt: Photorealistic 35mm film still. Match ONLY the look of the reference frames (warm tungsten work lamps, cream quilted padded fabric, metal ring frames, the white-and-orange Berkut suit and helmet, colour grade, film grain) -- do NOT copy their scale, the tube in the references is far too big. NOT a drawing. TRUE SCALE, extremely tight: the Voskhod 2 inflatable airlock is a padded tube only 1.0 metre across and 2.5 m long, barely bigger than a person, like a sleeping bag or an MRI bore. Cosmonaut Alexei Leonov in a swollen white Berkut spacesuit with orange-red straps, white helmet with red CCCP, backpack, lies stretched out LENGTHWISE along the tube axis, horizontal, like a hotdog in a bun, jammed in. His shoulders are 65 cm wide, two thirds of the tube diameter; the tube is only one and a half times as wide as his shoulders. His helmet almost touches the ceiling, his backpack scrapes the other side, both elbows press into and dent the padded walls. He CANNOT sit up, cannot turn sideways, there is NO empty space around him, no floor area, only a few centimetres of gap anywhere. He is twisting his torso and shoulders, trying to roll and fold his knees up toward his chest to turn round, straining. Face through the visor: drenched in sweat, exhausted, gritted teeth, visor misted at the edges. Camera: jammed up near the ceiling at the inner end by his boots, looking along his back toward the outer hatch. In the foreground his bent knees are pressed against both walls at once; in the middle his backpack and the back of his helmet, shoulders touching the walls on both sides; beyond his helmet the round outer hatch opening, barely wider than his shoulders, with black space and a sliver of blue Earth. His head is turned back over his shoulder toward camera, sweaty strained face visible through the visor. Padded quilted walls crowd every edge of the frame. 16:9.

Edit this photograph, keeping exactly the same photorealistic look: same warm tungsten lamps, same cream quilted padded fabric walls, same tight padded tube, same colour grade and film grain, same sweating grimacing face. NOT a drawing. Change the pose and layout: the cosmonaut is now stretched out LENGTHWISE along the tube axis, lying straight like a hotdog in a bun, NOT curled in a ball, NOT crouching: a 1.9 m man in a 2.5 m long tube that is only 1.0 m across. His legs extend toward the camera, his boots and shins in the near foreground, heavily foreshortened, knees slightly bent and pressing against the walls; his torso and backpack run away from camera along the tube; his helmet is at the far end. The tube is only about 1.5 times as wide as his shoulders: his shoulders almost span the tube, both elbows are bent outward and press into and dent the padded walls on left and right, his helmet nearly touches the ceiling. The round outer hatch is at the far END of the tube, directly beyond his helmet, on the tube axis, facing the camera (not on the side wall), its opening only slightly wider than his shoulders, black space and a sliver of blue Earth through it; he is reaching up toward its rim. Helmet lettering in Cyrillic: red "СССР". The white suit has orange-red harness straps and buckles, not racing stripes. Camera low at the inner end, just beyond his boots, looking straight along the tube. 16:9.

Photorealistic 35mm film still. From the reference photo take ONLY the look: warm tungsten cage lamps, cream quilted padded fabric, the white Berkut spacesuit with orange-red harness straps, white helmet with red Cyrillic СССР, the sweating grimacing face, colour grade and film grain. Do NOT copy its pose or its roomy tube. NOT a drawing. The Voskhod 2 Volga airlock as in the real museum trainer: a soft padded fabric cylinder only 1 metre in diameter and 2.5 m long, barely wider than a man in a swollen spacesuit, like a sleeping bag or a hot dog bun. Leonov lies perfectly STRAIGHT along the tube's axis like a hot dog in a bun: body fully extended, legs together and straight, boots together, right arm pressed tight along his side, left arm stretched straight ahead of him toward the hatch. He has NO room to bend his knees outward, spread his elbows, sit up or turn. The padded wall hugs him all round, touching and slightly squashed against his helmet, both shoulders, backpack, hips and boots; only a few centimetres of gap anywhere. The tube is only a little wider than his suit. The struggle is shown only by small movements: straining, one shoulder jammed into the padding, his outstretched glove pushing against the padding, drenched in sweat, grimacing, the visor fogged with condensation at the edges. No flags or national patches on the suit. Camera: at the open round outer end of the tube, looking straight in along the axis at him. His helmet and outstretched glove are nearest the camera, his face through the fogged visor, and the rest of his body recedes straight away behind his helmet, heavily foreshortened, toward the inner hatch. The circular padded cross-section wraps tightly around his helmet and shoulders, filling the frame edges with a ring of quilted padding and the metal hatch rim. 16:9.

steps.prompt: Photorealistic 35mm film still, NOT a drawing. Its walls are made rigid by air-filled tubes: inflatable ribs running LENGTHWISE along the wall, side by side all round the circumference, covered in pale tan fabric, so the chamber inside is only 1.0 m across, about the size of a phone booth laid on its side. Reference 2 gives the cosmonaut's pose and look: white Berkut spacesuit with orange-red harness straps, white helmet with red Cyrillic СССР, lying straight. Scene: INSIDE this airlock in orbit. The round cross-section of the chamber is only about 1.4 times as wide as his shoulders; the rounded lengthwise ribs press in on him all round. No lamps on the walls: cold blue-white Earthlight through the open outer hatch ring plus a dim warm glow from the capsule end. Leonov lies perfectly STRAIGHT along the tube axis like a hot dog in a bun: body fully extended, legs together and straight, boots together, arms tight along his sides; he cannot bend his knees out, spread his elbows, sit up or turn. The ribs touch his helmet, both shoulders, backpack, hips and boots, only a few centimetres of gap. The struggle shows only in small movements: straining, one shoulder jammed against a rib, a glove pushing against the wall, face drenched in sweat and GRIMACING with effort (not smiling), visor fogged with condensation at the edges. No emblems, patches or flags on the suit. Camera: inside the chamber just behind his boots, on the tube axis, looking along his body toward the open round outer hatch ring at the far end, black space and a thin sliver of blue Earth beyond. Boot soles together in the foreground, straight legs, hips, backpack and helmet running away down the middle, heavily foreshortened; the ring of lengthwise ribs converges in perspective around him, tight on every side. 16:9.

steps.prompt: Photorealistic 35mm film still, NOT a drawing. Reference 1 (museum photo of the real Voskhod 2 Volga airlock hatch) gives the TRUE tightness and construction: a thick maroon-brown foam padding ring gripping the cosmonaut's white helmet and shoulders with barely any gap, tan fabric behind it, grey riveted metal hatch ring. Reference 2 gives the photoreal look: the white Berkut spacesuit with orange-red harness straps, the white helmet with red Cyrillic СССР, the sweating, red, grimacing face with clenched teeth and furrowed brow, the film grade and grain. Leonov is jammed in so tight there is no room around him at all: the padding presses on his helmet and both shoulders on every side, dented around him. His visor is clear (or the gold sun visor raised) so his face shows: drenched in sweat, clenched teeth, furrowed brow, eyes squeezed, visor misted at its edges. One gloved hand is jammed flat against the padding by his chest; he is straining, trying to twist his shoulders. No lamps, no flags, no emblems or patches. Framing: seen from INSIDE the tube, a wide-lens close shot looking at him head-on along the tube axis. His helmet and shoulders fill the circular cross-section; the maroon-brown padded wall presses against his helmet and shoulders on every side and crowds every edge of the frame. No visible length of body, no space around him, only helmet, face, shoulders, chest and the jammed glove. Light: cold blue-white Earthlight from behind the camera plus a dim warm glow. 16:9.

steps.prompt: Photorealistic 35mm film still, NOT a drawing. Use the first reference image only for the cosmonaut's look: white Berkut spacesuit with orange-red harness straps, white helmet with red Cyrillic СССР, sweating red grimacing face with clenched teeth, film grade and grain. No flags or emblems. The Volga airlock interior (real 1965 design): the wall is pale off-white / light grey fabric lining in fine, dense, narrow lengthwise pleats (the 40 air-filled booms seen from inside), exactly like the interior in the construction photo reference, NOT fat cushions and NOT maroon foam; each end is a thick bronze-coloured bolted metal flange ring with rows of bolts; a thin maroon-brown foam padding collar only at the outer hatch rim; two small round lamps on the wall; a small grey duplicate control panel with a few toggle switches mounted on the wall near his hand. One end is a rigid metal ring with the round outer hatch, CLOSED; the other end is the capsule's round metal hatch. Inside diameter only 1.0 m, length 2.5 m; Leonov, 1.9 m long in his swollen suit, lies straight along it. Composition: a close SIDE view along his body inside the tube, camera low at his side at chest height. The ribbed pale fabric wall is only a few centimetres above his visor and curves down close on both sides, crowding the top of the frame. His gloved hand is pressed flat against the wall above his chest, fingers spread, denting the fabric. His face in three-quarter profile through a visor misted with condensation at its edges: sweating, clenched teeth, painful grimace. One small wall lamp near his head rakes warm light across the helmet, glove and the ribs of the fabric; deep shadows. The small grey control panel with toggle switches is on the wall just beyond his hand. His straight body and legs recede out of focus along the tube toward the capsule hatch. 16:9. The second reference (archive photo of the real airlock sections under construction) shows the true interior wall and flange rings only; do not include the engineers or the factory.
